```text
# PR #4902: Patch: an imagined opponent whose reply reaches its step cap still makes its attacks and ends its turn, where a five-use Activate now hides a lethal

Closes #4810

## What changed

The AI's model of its opponent's turn (`simulate_reply_with`, `crates/ai/src/reply.rs`) now keeps steps for its attacks and always ends its turn:

- **A cap on plays and Activates.** Known plays and visible Activates together take at most the new `AI_REPLY.play_steps` (6) of the reply's `max_steps` (12) steps. Past that, a step tries neither and goes on to Deft switches, attacks and Position switches as before.
- **Closing the turn.** If the 12 steps run out with the opponent still on turn, the reply ends that turn in up to `AI_REPLY.close_steps` (3) more steps: the endTurn plus the prompts the turn's end opens, each answered by `best_auto_answer`. The line is then scored at the AI's next decision, like every other reply.
  - Each of those steps costs a node, so a counter that runs dry there still returns `None`.
  - A refused endTurn still ends the reply where it stands.
- **Ruling R4810000** (`spec/rulings/R4810000.md`), with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/4810.md`.
- **Docs.** One sentence added to §9.9 "The opponent's reply" (`spec/09-architecture/9.9-practice-ai.md`), plus matching clauses in `crates/ai/README.md` and `docs/polish/3-ai.md`. Both constants have doc comments in `crates/ai/src/config.rs`.
- **Tests.** A new `mod step_caps_r4810000` in `crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs`:
  - `r4810000_a_free_activate_takes_at_most_play_steps_so_the_lethal_attacks_still_come` pins the issue's scene with a test-only free Activate ♾️ "Gain 1 Armor", so a balance patch cannot move it. The opponent gains 6 Armor, then three 4/4s kill the AI at 12, in 9 nodes.
  - `r4810000_a_reply_whose_steps_run_out_still_ends_the_opponents_turn` uses five Windfury 1/1s and the Armory. The reply makes 6 Armor uses and 6 attacks, then ends its turn. It returns at the AI's turn-11 main phase with no prompt, the AI at 24, in 13 nodes.
  - `r4810000_beside_a_miner_v5_the_reply_still_makes_its_lethal_attacks` is the issue's own board on seed `audit-reply-miner-7`, with and without S #66 Miner v5.

## How it was tested

- **New tests:** `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai r4810000` gave 3 passed.
  - With `play_steps: 12, close_steps: 0` (main's behaviour) all three fail. The Miner test fails with the issue's message: `["core-008","core-008","core-008","stinkyscape-066"]: active P2, turn 10, the AI at 2`. The config was then put back.
- **AI crate:** `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` passed: lib 66, `ai` 1051, `ai_slow` 102 (15 ignored, the existing daily ones).
- **Dependent crates:** `cargo test -p jackioh-server -p jackioh-shared -p jackioh-tools -p jackioh-wasm-core --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts` passed. All 19 test binaries were ok, 0 failed, and `apps/web/src/wire` has no diff.
- **Practice-claim fold:** `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server r1303002` gave 2 passed, with no re-record asked for.
- **Web:** `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh && pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/tutorial src/practice src/routes/practice` gave 43 files and 739 tests passed.
- **Checks:** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh spec check` (`2579 rulings … ok`), `patches check`, `catalog check` and `names --check` all passed. `classify --base origin/main --claims` classed the change as `Internal`.

## The screen (`training/improve.md`, A screen)

I ran `cargo jackioh arena --a self --b bin:<control> --set improve-dev`, with the control built from the base e3fe5705e3 before any edit.

- **Result:** 400 games, 199–201, edge −0.005 (−0.022 to 0.012), 3 decided of 200 (won 1, lost 2), 17 diverged. No game aborted, no simulation panicked, and every replay was ok.
- **Verdict:** `inconclusive: true` (R4319000), because 3 decided deals is below the 20 needed. An inconclusive screen neither keeps nor drops a change, so the scene tests settle it, as they did for R4433000.
- The result is recorded in the `play_steps` comment in `config.rs` and in the ruling's "Its values". The control binary has been deleted.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- **A count, not a share.** `play_steps` is a count of 6, not a share of `max_steps`. At 12 steps the two are the same, and a count says plainly what it holds back. 6 leaves one attack for each of a full row's `UNIT_ZONES` (5) Units plus the endTurn.
- **The closing steps are extra.** They come on top of the 12 rather than reserving the last of them. A reserved last step would leave unanswered any prompt the endTurn opens.
- **What `play_steps` counts.** Deft trials, Position switches and prompt answers are not counted: each is bounded by the Units on the field, or forced.
- **Rejected alternatives.** These are all recorded in R4810000:
  - Returning `None` at the cap: it reads as the counter running dry, and the line loses its score.
  - Raising `max_steps`: an unlimited Activate still crowds out the attacks, and every reply's worst case costs more nodes.
  - Attacking before Activates: R4515000's order lets an Activate that removes a Taunt go first.

## Where I departed from the plan

- I named the loop index `taken`, not `step`. The loop body later declares `let step = attack…`, which would shadow it.
- The plan put the §9.9 sentence in `spec/09-architecture.md`. That section now lives in `spec/09-architecture/9.9-practice-ai.md`, so the sentence went there. It reads "The opponent's turn there takes at most…" so it isn't mistaken for the AI's own line in the next sentence.

## Worth a second look

- **What else changes.** A reply whose endTurn landed on its last (12th) step and opened a prompt now answers that prompt during the closing steps. Before, it was handed back with the prompt still open. This is part of "ends its turn", but it is a second kind of reply that now plays differently, besides those with more than six plays and Activates.
```

````text
# #4810: Patch: an imagined opponent whose reply reaches its step cap still makes its attacks and ends its turn, where a five-use Activate now hides a lethal
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

### What happens

The opponent model's reply (`simulate_reply_with`, `crates/ai/src/reply.rs`) runs at most `AI_REPLY.max_steps` (12) steps. When it reaches the cap it returns `Some(current)` with the opponent still on turn (`reply.rs:911`, `:999`), and `replied_score` scores that state as a finished reply. Each step does one thing, in the order known play, visible Activate, Deft trial, attack (`reply.rs:936-959`), so what the cap cuts is the attacks.

Stinkyscape #66 Miner v5 ("Activate 5: Gain a random Stinkyscape Resource", no cost) is enough: each use gains a Resource, the Resource is a new instance and so not among the hidden cards, and `known_play` plays it on the next step. Five mines and five plays are ten of the twelve steps.

Board: the AI at 12 with no Unit; the opponent has three 4/4s and a Miner. Without the Miner the reply kills the AI. With it (seed `audit-reply-miner-7`, where the Resources are heals and 1-damage pings), the reply makes two attacks and then the loop runs out: the state handed back has no result, the opponent is still on turn 10, the AI is at 2 and one 4/4 has not swung. The line is scored as survived.

In a fuzz of 12 random-policy games, 5 of 154 replies stopped mid-turn this way, all with a Miner in play.

### What should happen

`reply.rs:887`: the reply runs "until the seat's next main phase or prompt, or game end". `crates/ai/src/config.rs` describes `max_steps` as covering "plays, attacks, prompt answers and the closing endTurn". `crates/ai/README.md` has the reply play the Activates it can see "then its attacks". A capped reply should still make its attacks and close the turn, or the cut should be reported so the line is not scored as answered.

### How to reproduce

Fails on `main` (3a83bd7): `a_five_use_activate_does_not_crowd_the_opponents_lethal_attacks_out_of_the_reply` in [`crates/ai/tests/audit_reply.rs` at bf24a52](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/bf24a52273bd5c0e7d6f9c740b28a8d7cb7f2b3e/crates/ai/tests/audit_reply.rs) (branch `claude/vigilant-mayer-pmyrhr`).

```rust
// handed_over_on(seed, p1, p2): a turn-9 scenario with p1 active, then p1's End turn through `reduce`.
#[test]
fn a_five_use_activate_does_not_crowd_the_opponents_lethal_attacks_out_of_the_reply() {
    let reply = |field: Value| {
        let state = handed_over_on("audit-reply-miner-7", json!({ "health": 12 }), json!({ "field": field }));
        let counter = create_node_counter(600, None);
        simulate_reply(&state, AI, &counter, &hidden_card_ids(&state, AI), Prices::NONE).expect("a reply")
    };
    let plain = reply(json!(["core-008", "core-008", "core-008"]));
    assert_eq!(plain.result.map(|result| result.winner), Some(Winner::from(HUMAN)));
    let mined = reply(json!(["core-008", "core-008", "core-008", "stinkyscape-066"]));
    let unswung = active_units_of(&mined, HUMAN).into_iter()
        .filter(|unit| unit.def_id == "core-008" && !unit.exertion.attacked).count();
    assert_eq!(mined.result.map(|result| result.winner), Some(Winner::from(HUMAN)),
        "beside a Miner v5 the reply stopped with the opponent still on turn: active {:?}, turn {}, \
         the AI at {}, {unswung} of the 4/4s unswung",
        mined.active, mined.turn, mined.players[AI].hero.health);
}
```

Output today: `beside a Miner v5 the reply stopped with the opponent still on turn: active P2, turn 10, the AI at 2, 1 of the 4/4s unswung`.

The test depends on its seed because the Resources are random; on other seeds the board still reaches lethal (fewer plays beat standing still). Pin the scene so a balance patch cannot move it (a stand-in with a free five-use Activate, if the testkit allows one).

### Where

The AI: `crates/ai/src/reply.rs` (`simulate_reply_with`'s loop and what it returns at the cap).

### Version or commit

`main` at 3a83bd7.

### Notes for the fix

- Cap the steps that are not attacks apart from the attacks (for example, stop trying known plays and Activates once a share of `max_steps` is spent), and when the cap is reached with the opponent still on turn, close the turn with `EndTurn` so the line is scored at the seat's next decision, as every other reply is.
- Any new number is a named constant in `AI_REPLY` (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
- `max_steps` appears in no test, in neither the README nor SPEC §9, and in no ruling, so nothing pins the cut; this is a decision the spec does not make, so it takes a ruling note in this issue's block.
- A change here moves what the reply plays on boards with many Activates, so fixed-seed AI games can move. `training/improve.md` says how a change to the AI's play is screened; say in the pull request what was measured.
- Not among the findings of the AI audit tracker #4787.
````
